Hi Jared — thanks for sending this over. We completed the questionnaire and attached a short answers workbook plus a high-level dataflow diagram for your reviewers. Highlights below (full answers attached):

1) Where data is stored (hosted API)- Primary request processing and short‑term caches are provisioned in the region you choose at sign‑up. For Aurametrics (US-west), primary compute and ephemeral KV caches will live in US‑West (Oregon). Redundant logs and audit records for the hosted plane are replicated to a secondary region for resilience (US‑East).

2) Default retention windows- Ephemeral request tokens / in-memory KV cache: retained for up to 2 hours by default (configurable).- Short-term request logs (used for debugging/tracing): default 30 days.- Aggregated usage metrics and billing records: retained 13 months.

3) Deletion workflow- Customer‑initiated tenant erasure request -> validated by account owner -> queued by platform orchestration -> staged deletion of live keys and cached artifacts (minutes to hours) -> background purge of logs and backups per retention SLAs (up to 30 days for short logs, up to 90 days for snapshots if in progress). Formal completion confirmation is provided after background purge completes.

We noted a few questions on the form (cells highlighted) where we asked for specifics about Aurametrics’ required SLA for erasure confirmation and whether archived backups are considered in scope — happy to sync tomorrow to walk through.

Attached: Redwood_Questionnaire_Responses_20270509.xlsx, Redwood_HostedAPI_Dataflow_Diagram.svg

Hi Soojin/Ben,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the workbook. A couple of clarifications legal needs before we mark this complete: 
- You indicate a secondary replication to US‑East for resilience. Does Aurametrics have the option to restrict replication to a single region (no secondary replication) on our paid plan?

Hi Jared / Aurametrics Legal — Marissa from Security & Ops here. Following up with the explicit timelines and clarifications you requested. I kept this high‑level for procurement; happy to provide logs/evidence under an NDA or addendum.

Summary answers (concise):
- Regional replication controls: By default, Redwood configures a primary region + a single secondary region for high availability. For enterprise customers with dedicated commitments we offer a "region-lock" option: if selected at onboarding, no automatic cross‑region replication will occur and fallbacks are limited to the chosen region. This is available as part of our Dedicated/Private plans; for Hosted API customers we can offer a contract clause to limit replication to a single region on a case basis (requires a short compliance review).

- Snapshots/backups and erasure: Snapshots used for disaster recovery are stored encrypted and are on a 90‑day rotation by default. A tenant erasure request will remove live tenant data and expunge active caches immediately (minutes to hours). Snapshots are scheduled for purge at their next rotation window; if Aurametrics requires accelerated purge we will commit to a targeted 45‑day maximum for snapshot deletion after a confirmed erasure request (subject to signed addendum).

- Audit logs / PII handling: Audit logs that contain PII are treated according to the same erasure request process for live data; however, for forensic/audit preservation there is a short reconciliation window (up to 7 days) before final purge to ensure integrity of compliance investigation. If you require stricter handling, we can include a clause to minimize that reconciliation window to 24 hours for covered log types.

Expected timelines (example workflow):
- Immediate: Validate request and pause writes to tenant (0–1 hour)
- Short term: Remove live keys, KV cache, and ephemeral artifacts (within 0–6 hours)
- Background: Purge short logs (within 30 days)
- Snapshots: Purge at rotation (default 90 days) or accelerated to 45 days with addendum
- Confirmation: Redwood will send final completion notice once background purges and snapshot scheduling are complete (email confirmation within 60 days in default flow, 45 days if accelerated purge agreed)

Attachments: we can share a redacted audit log sample and an internal purge script checklist under NDA. Let me know if you want that delivered to legal ops or your security team.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Sr. Security & Ops, Redwood Inference
